replication.target_description: Main replication Pearson correlation between ERN amplitude and error-potentiated startle magnitude, p. 4 section 4.2; later median-split, outlier-removal and combined-data analyses are distinct.

n.sample_role: Participants; 43 is a candidate final analysis sample, not explicitly a correlation-specific count.
n.exclusions: 51 recruited; eight excluded for high electrode impedances or excessive muscle artifacts. Additional correlation-specific exclusions not stated.
n.quote:
Eight subjects were excluded
from final analysis because impedances were too high (>5kΩ) in at least one of the elec-
trodes in which the statistical analyses were to be performed, or because of excessive
muscle artifacts. Thus, the final sample included in the analysis was 43 subjects.

es.quote:
The main finding of the original study, a correlation between ERN and EPS am-
plitude, did not reach the threshold for significance in our replication: r = -.25, p =
.11, one-tailed.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a 10-page completed primary report titled Replication of “Errors Are Aversive” by Greg Hajcak & Dan Foti (2008, Psychological Science), authored by Melissa Lewis and Michael Pitts. Title, authors and replicated study match the neutral reference; author order differs. No project DOI/OSF identifier or report date is printed, so these identifiers cannot be independently confirmed. Actual sample, results, discussion and figures establish a completed report rather than merely a preregistration. No PDF supplied. Only n_r and es_value_r assigned; all other fields are placeholders. Main replication correlation is r = -.25, with same-test p = .11, one-tailed (p_r unassigned). Candidate final sample is 43 participants, with 51 recruited and eight exclusions, but critical correlation N is not explicitly stated; nearby tests have t(40) and t(28). No N inferred from df, p, or combined N of 74. Later subgroup r = -.63, outlier-excluded r = -.20 and combined-data r = -.29 are separate analyses.
